methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + similar-valuation-tier peers in AI & Software. Range: $29.0B - $312.5B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in AI & Compute

data.narrative:
Waymo, a private AI & Software company founded by Sebastian Thrun and Anthony Levandowski, is valued at $126B with $16B+ raised to date. The valuation assessment draws on a peer set of 3 same-sector, similar-tier companies spanning both public and private stages: Palantir (public, $312.5B), Figure AI (Series C, $39.0B), and Scale AI (Series B, $29.0B).

The peer-median method is the applicable triangulation approach here. The median valuation across these three comparables is $39.0B, with a range spanning $29.0B to $312.5B. This wide spread reflects the heterogeneity in company maturity and scale within the AI & Software sector; the public peer (Palantir) commands a substantial premium, while the Series-stage peers cluster more tightly around the $29–39B band. Given limited methodological overlap and a single primary valuation method, the analysis yields a narrow implied range of $33.1B to $44.9B, centered on the peer median of $39.0B.

The current $126B valuation substantially exceeds the peer-derived range, suggesting either a significant private-to-public premium, sector-specific optionality priced into Waymo's terms, or a divergence in growth and profitability expectations relative to comparable firms. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the three-peer universe and the degree to which autonomous vehicle technology justifies a valuation multiple above established AI software peers. The analysis supports a valuation near $39.0B absent further methodological inputs.
